title: Grade 11 Biology National Exam & Practice 2018 (6 Chapters Combined)
description: Comprehensive examination bank combining 6 chapters (100 questions). Official Ethiopian national curriculum.

questions.questionText: What does the development of new devices by imitating biological structures indicate?
options: Most biological structures are based on the shape of technological innovations.
Close observations of biological structures can inform technological innovations.
The function of a technological product imitated from a biological structure is unrelated latter.
The design biological structures to technological tools for their intended function are ineligible.
questions.explanation: Imitating biological structures to create new devices (biomimicry) demonstrates how observing nature and biological structures directly inspires and informs technological advances.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following options contains a pair of innate and acquired animal behaviors?
options: Web making in spiders and honeybees dancing
Opening of mouth in chicks and honeybees dancing
Insight learning in monkeys and sensitization in sea slug
Nest-building in birds and habituation in prairie dogs
questions.explanation: Nest-building in birds is an innate (instinctive) behavior, whereas habituation in prairie dogs is an acquired (learned) behavior.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following characteristics correctly compares invertebrates and vertebrates? Invertebrates
options: are symmetrical, but vertebrates are necessarily asymmetrical.
are aquatic animals while vertebrates are terrestrial.
have closed, but vertebrates have open circulatory system.
do not regulate their body temperature while vertebrates do.
questions.explanation: Invertebrates are generally ectothermic (poikilothermic) and do not regulate their internal body temperature thermally, whereas endothermic regulation (warm-bloodedness) is characteristic of major vertebrate groups like birds and mammals.

questions.questionText: Which of the following descriptions is correct about the reproductive characteristics of rats, birds, frogs, and crocodiles?
options: Rats are mammals giving birth to a young child and are breast feeding.
Crocodiles lay eggs following an external fertilization in waterbodies.
The young hatching from a frog egg possesses the same permanent adult structures.
Birds are similar to frogs in that both lay eggs following an external fertilization.
questions.explanation: Rats are placental mammals that give birth to live young offspring and feed them milk via mammary glands (breast feeding/lactation).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of the economic importance of insects in agriculture and food production? Their role as
questions.explanation: Insects play a critical direct role in agriculture as key plant pollinators for crops and as nutrient-dense food sources (entomophagy) in food production systems.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements correctly describes how enzymes speed up the rate of chemical reactions? By
options: lowering the energy of reactants required to react more easily
decreasing the collision between substrate and enzyme
increasing the concentrations of reactants and speeding the reaction
being part of the reactants and product in a reaction
questions.explanation: Enzymes act as biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions by lowering the activation energy required for the reactants to reach the transition state.

questions.questionText: Assume that a protein has many binds and twists due to interaction between the side chain groups of amino acids to gain maximum stability. To which structure this protein belongs?
questions.explanation: The tertiary structure of a protein is defined by three-dimensional folding, bends, and twists resulting from interactions among the R-groups (side chains) of amino acids.

questions.questionText: What happens following a successful enzyme-substrate binding?
options: The activation energy of the reaction will be raised.
Loss of the molecular structure of the active site.
The substrate will become more stable.
questions.explanation: When a substrate molecule binds specifically to the active site of an enzyme, it forms a temporary intermediate known as the enzyme-substrate complex.

questions.questionText: During an experiment a student noticed that doubling the substrate concentration initially increases the rate of reaction, however, the rate remains the same up on addition of extra substrates. Why did this happen? Because the
options: active site of the enzyme was saturated.
reaction rate didn't attain the maximum rate.
questions.explanation: When all available active sites on the enzyme molecules are occupied by substrate molecules, the enzyme is saturated, causing the reaction rate to plateau at its maximum velocity ($V_{\max}$).

questions.questionText: What is the main purpose of malting in alcoholic production? To
options: remove the fibers in the grain to that interferes with clarification
activate enzymes that hydrolyze starch into monosaccharides
kill spoilage microorganisms that can affect the flavor of the product
initiate fermentation of sugars before application of the yeasts
questions.explanation: Malting involves germinating grains to activate endogenous amylase enzymes that break down complex starches into fermentable simple sugars (monosaccharides/disaccharides).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about Rh incompatibility? It refers to the
options: agglutination of blood from two sources with regard to the 'A' and 'B' antigens on erythrocytes.
Rh⁻ mother's antibodies attack the red blood cells of an Rh⁺ fetus.
absence of an agglutination when 'O' blood type is donated to all other blood types.
condition when an erythrocyte has neither the 'A' nor the 'B' antigen.
questions.explanation: Rh incompatibility occurs when an Rh-negative mother produces antibodies against the Rh-positive red blood cells of her fetus, leading to hemolytic disease of the newborn.

questions.questionText: A sequence of events that take place in a parent cell as a means of distributing genetic material to form daughter cells is
questions.explanation: The cell cycle is the ordered series of events that leads to cell duplication and division into daughter cells.

questions.questionText: In mice, the allele for black fur is dominant (B) over the allele for white fur (b), and the allele for short tail is dominant (S) over the allele for long tail (s). If the heterozygous genotypes of the two traits were crossed with each other and produced a total of 160 offsprings, how many offsprings with white fur long tail would be obtained?
questions.explanation: A dihybrid cross ($BbSs \times BbSs$) produces phenotypic ratios of 9:3:3:1. The double recessive phenotype (white fur, long tail: $bbss$) represents $\frac{1}{16}$ of the offspring. $\frac{1}{16} \times 160 = 10$ offspring.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following human genetic disorders is correctly matched with its example?
questions.explanation: Haemophilia is a classic example of an X-linked recessive genetic disorder. Cystic fibrosis is autosomal recessive, Down syndrome is a chromosomal disorder (trisomy 21), and albinism is an autosomal recessive condition.

questions.questionText: Suppose you have given a codon with base sequences of "CAA" which is responsible coding for an amino acid "glutamine". After exposure to a mutagenic agent its base sequence is changed to "CAG" but this still coding for the same amino acid "glutamine". What type of mutation has occurred in the base sequence?
questions.explanation: A mutation that alters a nucleotide base pair without altering the amino acid sequence of the resulting protein is called a silent mutation.

questions.questionText:
A teacher demonstrated two permanent microscopic glass slides of onion epidermal cells at different stages of cell division.

Slide X- was with paired homologous chromosomes arranged at the equator.

Slide Y- contained two haploid daughter cells with non-separated sister chromatids.

Based on the above information, to which phases and types of cell division do slides X and Y corresponded, respectively?
options: Metaphase II of meiosis and telophase II of meiosis
Metaphase I of meiosis and telophase II of meiosis
Metaphase I of meiosis and telophase I of meiosis
Metaphase of mitosis and telophase of mitosis
questions.explanation: Slide X shows homologous chromosome pairs aligned at the equatorial plate, which is characteristic of Metaphase I of meiosis. Slide Y shows two haploid cells forming where sister chromatids remain attached, which corresponds to Telophase I of meiosis.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the main role of mRNA during protein synthesis?
options: Translating DNA and relocate the information to the cytoplasm.
Bringing the transcribed information from the nucleus to the cytoplasm.
Assembling the synthesized amino acids into functional proteins.
Bringing the free amino acids located in the cytoplasm to the ribosome.
questions.explanation: Messenger RNA (mRNA) carries the genetic code transcribed from DNA in the nucleus out into the cytoplasm, where ribosomes use it to build proteins.

questions.questionText: In a test cross, the genotype of unknown organism cross with
questions.explanation: A test cross involves breeding an individual showing a dominant phenotype (whose exact genotype is unknown) with an individual expressing the homozygous recessive genotype to determine whether the first organism is homozygous or heterozygous.

questions.questionText:
Two women visited health a center to get information about the types of contraceptives and to choose the long lasting and reversible contraceptive methods, but with different mechanisms of actions.

 Woman I preferred the method that inhibits ovulation, while woman II preferred the one that prevents implantation. Based on this information, which of the following contraceptive were selected by woman I and II, respectively?
questions.explanation: Depo-Provera (an injectable hormonal contraceptive) is long-acting, reversible, and primarily functions by inhibiting ovulation. An Intrauterine Device (IUD) is long-acting, reversible, and acts primarily by preventing implantation/fertilization.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following components of the human musculoskeletal systems and its functions is correctly paired?
options: Tendon - keeps bones in a place and enables movements
Connective tissues - favor positions and movements
Joint and cartilage - connect tissues to tissues
questions.explanation: Connective tissues (including bones, cartilage, tendons, and ligaments) provide support, structure, and facilitate body positioning and movements. (Note: Tendons attach muscle to bone, and ligaments attach bone to bone).

questions.questionText:
Suppose the skeletal muscle was stimulated during a laboratory exercise and the following features were recorded.

I. Calcium ions bind to troponin

II. The nerve impulse reaches neuromuscular junction

III. Calcium ions reabsorbed into sarcoplasmic reticulum

IV. Myosin cross bridge with actin using ATP

In which of the following sequences do the muscles contract?
questions.explanation: Muscle contraction follows this sequence: (II) nerve impulse arrives at the neuromuscular junction → (I) calcium ions are released and bind to troponin → (IV) myosin heads bind to actin cross-bridges using ATP → (III) calcium ions are reabsorbed back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum during relaxation.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of sperm formation in human?
options: Germ cells → spermatogonia → primary spermatocyte → secondary spermatocyte → spermatids → spermatozoa
Germ cells → spermatogonia → spermatozoa → primary spermatocyte → secondary spermatocyte → spermatids
Primordial germ cells → primary spermatocyte → secondary spermatocyte spermatogonia → spermatozoa → spermatids
Primordial germ cells → spermatogonia → primary spermatocyte → secondary spermatocyte → spermatozoa → spermatids
questions.explanation: Spermatogenesis begins with undifferentiated germ cells/spermatogonia, which mature into primary spermatocytes, undergo Meiosis I to form secondary spermatocytes, complete Meiosis II to form spermatids, and finally differentiate into mature spermatozoa.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following causes of infertility in female when she decided not to have any more children?
questions.explanation: Voluntary sterilization (such as tubal ligation) is a permanent surgical method chosen by individuals who do not wish to have any more children.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following factors impairs safe decision making and contribute directly to the increased spread of sexually transmitted diseases (STI)?
options: Having no prior history of STI
questions.explanation: Misuse of recreational drugs alters judgment, self-control, and critical thinking, directly impairing safe decision-making and leading to high-risk sexual behaviors that increase STI transmission.

questions.questionText: A 19 years old girl who had unwanted sexual contact and harassed, became very emotional and mentally stressed. Which type of harmful traditional practice did the girl face?
questions.explanation: Unwanted sexual contact and harassment directed at an individual based on their gender constitute gender-based violence (GBV), leading to severe emotional and psychological distress.

questions.questionText: The ministry of Agriculture provided selected fish species for the farmers to introduce into two different ponds. Pond I had limited resources available, while pond II had unlimited resources. What types of growth patterns would be expected in the two ponds after a year?
options: Pond I would exhibit logistic growth while pond II an exponential growth.
The growth rate curve for pond I would be J-shaped while for pond II it would be S-shaped.
The growth curves in both pond I and pond II would be J-shaped.
Pond I would exhibit exponential growth while pond II a logistic growth.
questions.explanation: Limited resources cause population growth to level off at a carrying capacity (logistic/S-shaped growth), whereas unlimited resources allow unrestricted exponential growth (J-shaped growth).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following options correctly differentiates renewable and non-renewable resources?
options: Renewable resources can be exhausted after continuous utilization while non-renewable resources can't.
The rate of consumption of renewable resources exceeds its rate of recovery while non-renewable resources is lower.
Non-renewable resources are not susceptible to depletion due to over used while renewable resources can be depleted.
The quantity of renewable resources is not affected by human consumption while non-renewable resources is affected.
questions.explanation: Renewable resources (such as solar or wind energy) naturally replenish faster than or independently of human consumption rates, whereas non-renewable resources exist in finite quantities and deplete as humans consume them.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about the conservation mechanism of wild life?
options: Indigenous practices relay on the use of taboos for conservation of plants.
Modern practices relay on growing invasive plants in mountainous area in order to prevent soil erosion.
Controlled wildlife hunting areas can't be considered one of the conservation mechanisms.
Wild life conservation is selective protection of a species with economic significances and eliminating less valued species.
questions.explanation: Indigenous conservation strategies traditionally rely on social norms, sacred groves, and cultural taboos to restrict the exploitation of specific plant and animal species.

questions.questionText: Why are the chlorofluorocarbons considered to be the major cause of ozone layer depletion? Because they
options: prevent the formation of catalytic cycle of chlorine to form ozone layer.
increase the ozone's ultraviolet radiation-absorbing capacity.
cause chemical reactions that break down ozone molecules.
react with hydrogen ions to form hydrochloric acids in the ozone layer.
questions.explanation: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) release chlorine radicals under ultraviolet light, which catalyze chemical reactions that break down ozone ($O_3$) into oxygen molecules ($O_2$).

questions.questionText:
This item is based on the following given list of conservation method of plants

1. Relying on taboos for using some plant species

2. Establishing botanical gardens to maintain endangered species

3. Use of sacred places for protection of plants

4. Traditional agroforestry system practices

5. Use of preserving seeds in a genes bank

Based on the above information, which alternatives contains only indigenous knowledge?
questions.explanation: Items 1 (taboos), 3 (sacred sites), and 4 (traditional agroforestry) are traditional indigenous practices. Botanical gardens (2) and gene banks (5) represent modern scientific ex-situ conservation methods.

questions.questionText: Which of the following describes the tertiary structure of a protein?
options: The linear sequence of amino acids.
The interaction of multiple polypeptide subunits.
The overall 3D shape stabilized by R-group interactions.
The local folding into helices and sheets.
questions.explanation: Tertiary structure is the comprehensive, final three-dimensional shape of a single polypeptide chain, resulting from interactions between the amino acid side chains (R-groups).

questions.questionText: In the systematic naming of enzymes, assume an enzyme is designated as EC 3.4.11.1. Which of the following correctly describes this enzyme?
options: 4 - shows to which main class the enzyme belongs.
3 - indicates a subclass to which the enzyme belongs.
11 - gives a sub-subclass to which the enzyme belongs.
1 - a reference of its enzyme commission.
questions.explanation:
The Enzyme Commission (EC) number is a numerical classification system for enzymes.
 The four numbers represent a hierarchy: Class.Subclass.Sub-subclass.Serial Number.
 The first digit, 3, indicates the main enzyme class (in this case, 'Hydrolases').
 The subsequent numbers define the reaction with increasing specificity.

questions.questionText: A major negative impact of technology on society is often the promotion of a sedentary lifestyle, which can lead to:
options: Increased prevalence of non-communicable diseases like obesity and diabetes.
questions.explanation: While technology offers many benefits, its convenience can encourage inactivity, which is a known societal contributor to chronic health issues.

questions.questionText: An example of a technology directly inspired by the self-cleaning mechanism of the lotus leaf would be in the design of:
questions.explanation: The 'Lotus effect' describes the superhydrophobicity (extreme water repellency) and self-cleaning properties of the leaf, which has been imitated in coating technologies.

questions.questionText: A drug efficacy test was conducted under similar set up on two groups of infected mice (A and B). Group A were the control whereas group B were experimental group. A student gave a placebo to the control group and the drug to the experimental group. At the end, the experimental group got better. Which one of the following is true about the result?
questions.explanation: Since the control group received a placebo and did not improve while the experimental group received the drug and got better under the same conditions, the improvement can be attributed to the drug. Therefore, the drug has an effect.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following alternatives the whole list contains characteristics of animals?
questions.explanation:
Animals are heterotrophic (obtain food from other organisms), excrete metabolic wastes, exhibit motility (ability to move), and grow.

 They are multicellular and reproduce sexually, but not autotrophic. Therefore, option C correctly lists characteristics of animals.

questions.questionText: The term for a tool used to solve day-to-day biological tasks and support the discovery of more information in the course of biological studies is a:
questions.explanation: Biotechnological devices (or instruments) are tools used to solve day-to-day biological tasks and support the discovery of more information during biological studies.

questions.questionText: What is the collective term for the protective and nutrient layers added to the zygote to form the egg in birds and crocodiles?
questions.explanation: Internal fertilization is followed by the formation of the protective shell and provision of nutrients (yolk and albumen) before the egg is laid.

questions.questionText: Why must scientific inquiry remain ethically conscious when conducting studies on living organisms?
options: To ensure the final product is more profitable.
To comply with legal requirements and respect the values and rights of all life forms.
To speed up the research process.
To make the results more complex.
questions.explanation: Ethical consciousness is required to ensure compliance with laws and to respect the values, rights, and humane treatment of all life forms involved in the study.

questions.questionText: What is the collective term for the protein component of an enzyme?
questions.explanation: The Apoenzyme is the protein component of an enzyme. It is catalytically inactive by itself and requires the binding of a non-protein cofactor to become the active holoenzyme.

questions.questionText: A mother milks her cow every morning and the milk usually forms curd after three days. What is the first step to investigate why this change happens?
options: Take action to prevent the milk from curdling
Read scientific articles about the reason for curdling of milk
Formulate hypothesis about the reason for milk curdling
Ask a question why the milk forms curd
questions.explanation:
The first step in a scientific investigation is to identify and ask a question about the observed phenomenon.
 In this case, the investigation begins by asking why the milk forms curd.

questions.questionText: The function of osmoreceptors in the body is to sense changes in the concentration of:
questions.explanation: Osmoreceptors are specialized cells that detect changes in the concentration of water and electrolytes, helping to regulate osmoregulation.

questions.questionText:
The following are reaction types catalyzed by different classes of enzymes:

 1. Transferring hydrogen and oxygen atoms.

 2. Changing of the molecular form of the substrate.

 3. Joining of two molecules by the formation of new bonds.

 Which classes of enzymes catalyze the above reactions according to their consecutive order?
questions.explanation:
1. Transferring H and O: Oxidoreductases (involved in redox).

2. Changing molecular form: Isomerases (rearrange atoms). 

3. Joining two molecules: Ligases (form new bonds using ATP).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a general characteristic of animals?
options: They are heterotrophic and ingest their food
They have cell walls composed of cellulose
They are motile at some stage of their life cycle
questions.explanation: Animal cells lack cell walls; cell walls composed of cellulose are characteristic of plants. Animals are multicellular, eukaryotic, heterotrophic, and generally motile.

questions.questionText: Which term best describes the general feeling of disrespect for the rights and values of a living organism during a biological study?
questions.explanation: The unit directly refers to disrespectful acts to the values and rights of someone (including living organisms) as a component of ethical issues.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about the description of the cell theory?
options: Virchow stated that cell is the unit of structure, physiology and reproduction of living things.
Schleiden and Schwann stated that all cells come from pre-existing cells.
spontaneous generation theory states that all cells have basically different chemical composition.
Modern cell theory states that cells contain hereditary information that passes from cell to cell.
questions.explanation:
The Modern Cell Theory incorporates the original tenets and adds that cells carry hereditary information (DNA) which is passed from the parent cell to the daughter cells during division.

 Option A incorrectly attributes the combination of structure, physiology, and reproduction to Virchow (he primarily contributed the idea that cells come from pre-existing cells).

 Option B describes Virchow's contribution, not Schleiden and Schwann's original part.

 Option C is entirely incorrect as the spontaneous generation theory was disproved.

questions.questionText: The development of self-healing materials by scientists, inspired by the way organisms repair their own tissues, is a direct result of which concept?
questions.explanation: Imitating the functional mechanisms of nature, such as tissue repair, to create new materials is the definition of biomimicry.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an aquatic invertebrate that often undergoes asexual reproduction by budding?
questions.explanation: Budding is a common form of asexual reproduction in invertebrates like Hydra, where a new organism develops from an outgrowth or bud on the parent.

questions.questionText: From the following options, which one contains the steps of writing a scientific report in the correct order?
options: Title --> Hypothesis --> Procedure --> Prediction --> Results --> Conclusion --> Evaluation --> Acknowledgement
Title --> Hypothesis --> Prediction --> Evaluation --> Results --> Procedure --> Conclusion --> Acknowledgement
Title --> Hypothesis -->Prediction --> Procedure --> Results --> Conclusion --> Evaluation --> Acknowledgement
Title --> Prediction --> Hypothesis --> Procedure --> Evaluation --> Conclusion --> Results --> Acknowledgement
questions.explanation: The correct order of a scientific report is: Title, Hypothesis, Prediction, Procedure (method), Results, Conclusion, Evaluation, and finally Acknowledgement.

questions.questionText: Which of the following describes a key way Society influences the Science-Technology cycle?
options: Society prevents any new scientific discoveries.
Society only benefits from technology and never demands anything.
Societal needs and demands drive the direction of scientific research and technological development.
Society is completely separate from both science and technology.
questions.explanation: The diagram illustrates that Society demands more from both Science and Technology, driving the cycle of innovation and application to address human needs.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT the function of the plasma membrane in eukaryotic cells?
options: Transferring chemical energy from carbohydrates to ATP
Isolating the cell from the external environment
questions.explanation: The process of transferring chemical energy from carbohydrates to ATP (cellular respiration) primarily occurs in the mitochondria, not the plasma membrane.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of Biotechnology?
options: Using yeast to ferment beer or bake bread.
questions.explanation: Biotechnology involves the use of living organisms or biological systems (like yeast) to create products (food, beverages).

questions.questionText: During the light-independent reactions of photosynthesis
options: GP is reduced to TP by reduced NADP.
some of the GP is used to regenerate RuBP.
RuBP reacts with CO₂ to directly form TP.
glucose is directly produced from GP.
questions.explanation:
Glycerate-3-phosphate (GP) is reduced to Triose Phosphate (TP, or G3P) using the energy from ATP and the reducing power of NADPH (or reduced NADP).

 Option B is also true, but A is a primary step.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is considered an ethical issue related to human biological rights?
options: Whether or not to use a thermometer.
Questions about unfair discrimination based on genetic information.
The color of a laboratory coat.
questions.explanation: Ethical issues in biology are concerned with respecting the values for all life forms, and this includes determining the right or wrong values that may affect human rights to equality to live freely and naturally, such as preventing genetic discrimination.

questions.questionText:
This item is based on the following examples of genetic inheritance patterns:

1 Inflated and pinched pod forms will have inflated pod form.

2 Red cow and white bull will have roan calf.

3 AA and BB blood type people will have a child with AB blood type.

4 Red and white roses will have a pink rose offspring.

From the above patterns of inheritance, which of the following are exemplary for nonMendelian inheritance?
questions.explanation:
Non-Mendelian inheritance includes patterns other than simple dominant-recessive:
- 2 (roan coat color) – example of codominance.
- 3 (AB blood type) – example of codominance in human blood groups.
- 4 (pink rose from red and white) – example of incomplete dominance.
Example 1 (inflated and pinched pod) follows Mendelian dominant-recessive inheritance, so it is not non-Mendelian.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the best definition of Biotechnology according to the unit's context?
options: The use of biology to develop new products, methods, and organisms intended to improve human health and society.
The study of living organisms from the simplest to the most complex ones.
The sum of techniques, skills, and processes used in the production of goods or services.
The imitation of engineering systems from the structures of inanimate objects.
questions.explanation: Biotechnology is defined as the use of biological systems or living organisms and derivatives thereof, to make or modify products or processes for a specific use, as stated in the unit summary.

questions.questionText: The development of synthetic biology, which aims to create artificial biological parts or systems, is a result of the tight blending of:
questions.explanation: The blending of biology and technology forms biotechnology, and synthetic biology is a field within biotechnology that involves the design and construction of new biological entities.

questions.questionText: Suppose you did an experiment in a biology laboratory and need to report your work to your biology teacher. Which one of the following steps is correct to report the finding?
options: Title -> Procedure -> Result -> Hypothesis -> Prediction -> Evaluation
Title -> Hypothesis ->  Procedure -> Prediction -> Conclusion -> Result
Title -> Hypothesis -> Prediction -> Procedure -> Result -> Conclusion
Title -> Prediction -> Procedure -> Hypothesis -> Result -> Conclusion
questions.explanation: The correct order to report a scientific experiment is: start with the Title, state the Hypothesis, make a Prediction, describe the Procedure, present the Results, and end with the Conclusion.

questions.questionText: The following table compares prokaryotes and eukaryotes. In the above table, X, Y, and Z can be respectively stated as (X=DNA, Y=Mitochondria, Z=Ribosomes)
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText:
Four students wanted to conduct chemical tests on unknown food particles and used the following chemicals and materials:

 Student A: Test tubes and biuret solution.

 Student B: Test tubes, ethanol, water, filter paper.

 Student C: Test tubes, benedict's solution, water bath.

 Student D: Test tubes and iodine solution.

 Which of the above students planed a test for lipids?
questions.explanation: "Student B planned the lipid test because the ethanol and water procedure is used in the emulsion test for lipids, where a milky white emulsion indicates the presence of fats.

questions.questionText: In the Nitrogen Cycle, the process of Denitrification returns nitrogen to the atmosphere by converting:
questions.explanation: Denitrification is the final step in the nitrogen cycle, where anaerobic bacteria convert nitrates (NO3-) back into nitrogen gas (N2), completing the cycle and releasing the gas back into the atmosphere.

questions.questionText: The primary role of osmoregulation is to manage the concentration of:
questions.explanation: Osmoregulation controls the balance of water and electrolytes (salts) in the body to maintain stable conditions.

questions.questionText: What is the name for the inactive precursor form of a proteolytic enzyme that is stored in the pancreas to prevent self-digestion?
questions.explanation:
Digestive enzymes like trypsin and chymotrypsin are synthesized and stored as inactive zymogens (proenzymes), such as trypsinogen and chymotrypsinogen, respectively, to prevent the enzymes from breaking down the cells that produce them.

 They are activated only after secretion into the small intestine.

questions.questionText: In a biological study, Ethical Refinement means:
options: Replacing all animals with computer models.
Improving procedures and living conditions to minimize the pain and suffering of experimental animals.
Using an increased number of animals for more statistical power.
questions.explanation: Refinement is the 'R' principle focused on minimizing animal distress by improving all aspects of their housing and experimental procedures.

questions.questionText: What will happen to the reaction if you add a certain inhibitor or activator to the substrate having allosteric enzyme set up?
options: Inhibitor binds to active site to speed up the reaction.
Inhibitor binds to regulatory site to increase rate of reaction.
Activator binds to active site to initiate the reaction.
Activator binds to regulatory site to activate the reaction.
questions.explanation: Allosteric enzymes have a regulatory (allosteric) site separate from the active site. An activator binds to this site, causing a conformational change that enhances the enzyme's activity and increases the reaction rate. Inhibitors can also bind to the regulatory site but decrease activity.

questions.questionText: Why is the optimal temperature for human enzymes usually around 37 degrees Celsius?
options: It is the point where activation energy is highest.
It is the temperature that denatures the enzyme most quickly.
It is the normal physiological body temperature of humans.
It is the temperature where substrate molecules are least reactive.
questions.explanation: Enzymes have optimum conditions, and for human enzymes, the optimum temperature is typically the normal human body temperature (approximately 37 degrees Celsius) because they function most effectively to support metabolism at this temperature.

questions.questionText: The use of remote sensing satellites in biology to monitor deforestation or vegetation health is an example of:
questions.explanation: Remote sensing is a technological application used to gather environmental data for biological and ecological studies.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a consequence of a high population of a pest insect species?
options: Increased yield of commercial products like honey
questions.explanation: A high population of a pest insect can lead to extensive and harmful damage to agricultural crops, representing a negative economic impact.

questions.questionText: A silent mutation is a point mutation that:
options: Changes the amino acid to a stop codon.
Changes the amino acid to a different, less important one.
Changes a codon but does not change the amino acid sequence.
Causes a shift in the reading frame.
questions.explanation: Due to the redundancy of the genetic code, a silent mutation changes the DNA base pair and the mRNA codon, but the new codon still codes for the same amino acid, resulting in no change to the protein.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an industrial application of the enzyme protease?
options: Tenderizing meat and biological stain removal in detergents.
Treating starch to produce corn syrup.
questions.explanation: Proteases, or proteinases, break down proteins. In the food industry, they are used to tenderize meat. In the detergent industry, they are used in biological detergents to break down protein stains like blood and grass.

questions.questionText: An enzyme is said to be saturated when:
options: The temperature reaches its optimum value.
The product concentration begins to inhibit the reaction.
All of the enzyme's active sites are continuously occupied by substrate molecules.
The enzyme denatures due to low pH.
questions.explanation:
Enzyme saturation occurs when the concentration of the substrate is so high that all available active sites are bound to substrate molecules at any given moment.
 At this point, the reaction rate is at its maximum (Vmax).

questions.questionText: Which component of DNA is different between an Adenine nucleotide and a Cytosine nucleotide?
questions.explanation: All DNA nucleotides have the same deoxyribose sugar and phosphate group; they differ only in their Nitrogenous base (A, T, C, or G).

questions.questionText: What is the final product of translation?
questions.explanation: Translation is the process where the genetic code carried by mRNA is decoded by ribosomes to synthesize a polypeptide (protein) chain.

questions.questionText: The main difference between internal and external fertilization is the:
questions.explanation: Internal fertilization occurs inside the female's body, while external fertilization occurs outside the body, in the environment.

questions.questionText: If two genes are located very close together on the same chromosome, they are most likely to be inherited together. This phenomenon is called:
questions.explanation: Genetic linkage is the tendency of genes that are located close together on the same chromosome to be inherited together during meiosis.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an autosomal dominant genetic disorder?
options: Sickle Cell Anemia (recessive inheritance pattern is most significant)
questions.explanation: Huntington's Disease is an example of an autosomal dominant disorder, meaning only one copy of the defective gene is required to cause the disorder.

questions.questionText: What is the effect of doubling the concentration of a competitive inhibitor in a fixed-enzyme, fixed-substrate system?
options: The proportion of inhibited enzyme decreases.
The proportion of enzyme bound to the inhibitor increases.
questions.explanation:
Increasing the concentration of a competitive inhibitor increases its chance of binding to the active site, thereby increasing the proportion of inhibited enzyme.

 Kinetically, competitive inhibition increases the apparent Km (lowers the apparent affinity) but does not change Vmax.

questions.questionText:
A student conducted an experiment using different enzymes to assess the enhancement of reaction rates under different conditions. She represents her results as indicated in the following table:

| Enzymes used | Cofactors used | Rate enhancement | Optimum temperature required °C 

Which one of the following is an acceptable conclusion of the experiment?
options: The rate enhancement for enzymes 'Z' is less because it didn't use a cofactor.
The temperature increases the rate of chemical reaction decreases.
Enzyme 'Y' should be enhanced the rate better at temperature slightly higher than 37°C.
Enzyme 'M' cannot enhance the rate of reaction further if the temperature exceeds 30°C.
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: A person with blood type AB possesses which antibodies in their blood plasma?
questions.explanation: Type AB blood has both A and B antigens on the red blood cells, so the plasma contains neither Anti-A nor Anti-B antibodies to avoid self-aggression.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a primary role of protease enzymes in the industrial processing of leather?
options: Removing unwanted hair and non-collagenous proteins from the hide.
questions.explanation: In leather processing (tanning), proteases are used in the 'bating' step to remove residual hair, non-collagenous proteins, and other impurities, which softens the leather and prepares it for the tanning process.

questions.questionText: In a pedigree chart, a square symbol typically represents a:
questions.explanation: Standard pedigree notation uses a square to represent a male and a circle to represent a female.

questions.questionText:
This item is based on the following table on the function of cellular organelles:

Which numbers in the above table show the **correct function** of the given organelles?
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: The ultimate goal of Gene Therapy is to:
options: Correct genetic defects by introducing functional genes.
questions.explanation: Gene Therapy is a medical technique aimed at fixing genetic problems at their source by introducing a functional copy of a defective gene into a patient's cells.

questions.questionText: A key difference between the Lock-and-Key Model and the Induced-Fit Model is the consideration of the active site's:
questions.explanation: The core difference lies in the active site's state: Lock-and-Key assumes a rigid active site, while Induced-Fit recognizes the **flexibility** of the active site, allowing it to undergo a conformational change to precisely fit the substrate.

questions.questionText: Industries in the medicine sector use glucose oxidase in Clinistix strips for
options: easy diagnosis of diabetes by examining a urine sample.
restoring blood supply to areas of heart muscle.
detecting toxic metabolites in the blood.
questions.explanation:
Glucose oxidase is an enzyme used in Clinistix strips to detect glucose in urine.

 High glucose levels in urine indicate hyperglycemia, which helps in the diagnosis of diabetes.

questions.questionText: The enzymatic cleavage of lactose into glucose and galactose is catalyzed by which class of enzyme?
questions.explanation: The enzyme lactase (or beta-galactosidase) breaks the glycosidic bond in lactose by adding a water molecule (hydrolysis), which places it in the Hydrolase class.

questions.questionText: A change in a single nucleotide base pair of a gene is known as a:
questions.explanation:
A Point mutation is a change in a single base pair of DNA.

 This includes substitutions, which can be silent, missense, or nonsense.

questions.questionText: The two purine bases found in DNA are:
questions.explanation: Purines are nitrogenous bases with a double-ring structure. They are Adenine (A) and Guanine (G).

questions.questionText: In humans, the organ that plays an important role in osmoregulation by producing varying amounts of urine is the:
questions.explanation: The kidney is vital in osmoregulation in humans, producing a large amount of urine when there is excess water and a small amount when water is low to maintain balance.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a structural feature of an enzyme's active site?
options: It is a large, fully solvent-exposed surface area.
It is rigid and cannot change shape upon substrate binding.
It is composed of amino acid residues that may be far apart in the primary sequence.
It is primarily composed of lipid molecules.
questions.explanation: The active site is formed by the tertiary folding of the polypeptide chain, bringing together amino acid residues from distant parts of the primary structure to create a specific three-dimensional pocket.

questions.questionText: If the Km value for an enzyme is high, it indicates that the enzyme has a:
questions.explanation:
The Michaelis constant (Km) is inversely related to the enzyme's affinity for its substrate.

 A high Km means a high concentration of substrate is required to reach half Vmax, indicating a low affinity.

questions.questionText: The total collection of genes within a population is referred to as the:
questions.explanation: The Gene pool is the total aggregate of genes and their alleles present in a population at any given time.

questions.questionText: What is the key functional advantage of the multisubunit (quaternary) structure of an allosteric enzyme?
options: It makes the enzyme more resistant to denaturation.
It allows for cooperative binding and allosteric regulation.
It prevents the enzyme from being consumed in the reaction.
It increases the enzyme's solubility in water.
questions.explanation:
Allosteric enzymes are typically composed of multiple subunits (quaternary structure).

 This structure allows for the transmission of conformational changes between subunits upon regulatory (allosteric) effector binding, enabling cooperative binding and sensitive allosteric regulation.

questions.questionText: A genetic disorder characterized by a missing piece of the X chromosome, causing intellectual disability, is:
questions.explanation: Fragile X syndrome is a genetic disorder associated with a mutation on the X chromosome, typically involving a significant expansion of a CGG trinucleotide repeat.

questions.questionText: The process of a young animal forming a strong, early, and typically irreversible attachment to the first moving object it sees is called:
questions.explanation: Imprinting is a type of learned behavior that occurs during a critical period early in an animal's life.

questions.questionText: The structure of DNA is often described as a:
questions.explanation: DNA is a polymer made up of two strands twisted around each other to form a Double Helix.

questions.questionText: The design of a robotic arm that can flexibly grasp objects, inspired by the function of an elephant's trunk, is an example of biomimicry at which scale?
questions.explanation: The imitation can occur at macro (large) or nano (very small) scales, and a robotic arm is a large, functional mechanism.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences correctly describes the properties of water? It:
options: allows all light wavelengths to pass through its various depths.
requires high amount of energy to heat up.
contracts when it freezes and hence acts as an insulator.
takes low energy to change into vapor.
questions.explanation:
Water has a very high specific heat capacity. This means it requires a high amount of energy to heat up (or change its temperature).

 The high specific heat helps moderate temperatures on Earth.

questions.questionText: Which of the following external factors influence the turnover rate of enzymes by completely damaging their tertiary structure?
questions.explanation: Extreme temperature and extreme pH can denature enzymes by breaking the hydrogen bonds, ionic bonds, and other interactions that maintain their tertiary structure, permanently damaging the enzyme and stopping its activity.

questions.questionText: The structural level of a protein that is formed by the folding of a single polypeptide chain into a compact, three-dimensional shape, stabilized by R-group interactions, is the:
questions.explanation: The tertiary structure involves the overall three-dimensional shape of a single polypeptide chain, including the folding of secondary structures and the interactions between the side chains (R-groups) of the amino acids.
